title: The Urchins That Doubled
story: In the moonlit tidepools below Gullcliff, Saltrime the Doubling Urchin Bloom is spreading over the oyster beds the village depends on. Mr 6 counts 5 urchins at dusk, and the sea-wife warns him that their number doubles every 2 hours. Mr 6 sits on a wet rock with his sword across his knees and thinks before he swings.
question: If the doubling goes on unchecked, how many urchins will cover the oyster beds 10 hours after dusk?
solution: In 10 hours the bloom doubles 10 / 2 = 5 times.
After 10 hours there would be 160 urchins.
praise: Doubling was absolutely the right idea — the missing step was counting the doublings (10 hours ÷ 2 hours = 5), not 10 of them.
hint: How many 2-hour stretches fit inside 10 hours? That's how many times the bloom doubles.
victory: Mr 6 doesn't strike a single urchin — he simply opens the sluice and lets the cold current sweep the whole bloom out to sea, and Saltrime drifts away grumbling about mathematics.
imagePrompt: Mr 6, a walking numeral six knight with a blue cape, crouches thoughtfully on a kelp-slick rock above moonlit tidepools brimming with glowing spiny urchins forming a many-eyed bloom-creature, cool silver light and misty sea air.
